class: A script that sums token usage from a Claude Code transcript (.jsonl) line by line over-counts, because the transcript writes one line per content block of the same assistant message and every such line repeats the message's full usage; any per-line total (tokens, turns) is inflated by the blocks-per-message ratio, while a per-line average stays roughly right, which hides the error.
mechanism: Assistant messages with text + tool_use blocks are split into several .jsonl lines sharing one message.id, each carrying the identical usage object; summing usage per line counts that message 2-3 times.

first_seen.where: scripts/orchestrator/row_actuals.py:75-81 transcript_tokens (commit f441b87d), process-tools check in session 5db71e90
first_seen.evidence: newest real session .jsonl: tool total 408383 vs a per-message-id recount 176261 (124 assistant lines, 53 distinct ids, 42 ids repeated with identical usage); row 16 agent output: 1041991 vs 494203 (135 lines, 70 ids)

fix: Count usage once per message.id (keep the last line per id); a test feeds a transcript where one id appears three times. Swept: scripts/orchestrator/measure_process.py read_session (lines 152-155) counts turns and ctx per line too - same fix; its avg_ctx is ratio-stable, its turns/ctx totals are not.

detection.note: Found by an independent recount in a findings-only check. Guarded since 232f25d4: one helper (UsageOnce in measure_process.py, imported by row_actuals.py) counts usage once per message id; both test files feed one id on three lines. Real-data proof 2026-10-23: transcript 7a0c81e3 (415 usage lines, 188 ids) - tool 440947 = per-id input 378 + cache creation 321133 + output 119436.

occurrences.evidence: as first_seen; measure_process read_session sums per line (read of lines 149-163)
